Install & first login

A fresh Debian or Ubuntu VPS, about five minutes. Root or sudo, a systemd host, port 2095 free. The default install asks you nothing.

What you need

  • A Linux VPS — Debian or Ubuntu recommended.
  • Root, or an account with sudo.
  • A host with systemd (a VM or a bare-metal server).
  • Port 2095 free.

Release binaries

The installer downloads a release binary from GitHub Releases. The panel and its CLI ship from the same single binary, so there is no compile step, no git, no npm, no runtime packages on the box.

Install

The installer is the entry point and it is what your customers execute. Pinning the tag means a main change can never silently change what root runs. bash install.sh --help prints the full surface.

To walk through every setting instead of using the defaults, run interactive or --interactive. Setting OVM_REPO=myorg/OVManager points source downloads and update pulls at your own repository (for example a fork). -y skips the prompts.

Defaults

SettingDefault
Install modenative (systemd single binary)
Port2095
URL pathrandom, e.g. /dashboard/
Admin useradmin
Owner passwordnone — a one-time claim key is printed instead
TLSself-signed (encrypted; the browser warns once)

Every question has a default, so pressing Enter all the way through is a valid install. The installer writes /opt/ovmanager/.env with HOST, PORT, URLPATH, ADMIN_USERNAME and DATA_DIR, and starts the panel afterwards, which health-checks the first boot.

The public address for shared subscription links is optional. Set PUBLIC_URL=https://panel.example.com in .env (or pass OVM_ADMIN_PASS to ovmanager reset-password for a manual install) so subscription links work for users on any network.

First login: the claim flow

The installer never creates an owner password and never writes one to disk. It prints a one-time claim key. The owner account does not exist until a browser posts that key and chooses a password — there is no plaintext credential in your terminal scrollback or in any file. The key is spent the moment it works and the file holding it is deleted.

The Ready card at the end of the install shows something like:

Open    https://YOUR-SERVER-IP:2095/a1b2c3d4/claim
Claim key (one-time)  paste it in the browser
User    admin         set the password on first login

  1. Open the URL

    It ends in /claim. With the self-signed certificate the browser warns once — click Advanced, then Proceed.

  2. Paste the claim key

    Choose the owner password in the same form. At least 8 characters, and not a placeholder like change-me.

  3. You are signed in

    The password is stored as a bcrypt hash in the panel database, never in .env. Lost the key before claiming? Run sudo ovmanager owner-claim to mint a fresh one.

Update and uninstall

These live in ovmanager, which the installer adds and refreshes on every update — you do not re-download anything.

Updates stage the new tree, health-check it and roll back automatically if the new version does not come up. An update interrupted by a reboot is recovered on the next ovmanager update run. The database migrates itself on the next start.

Install with no terminal

A run without a terminal cannot ask, so it needs -y to say that is intended; without it the installer stops and says so. There is no menu on a non-tty.

The panel manages accounts; it does not carry VPN traffic. Install OVNode on the machine your users will connect to and register it under Adding nodes.

OVManager is MIT-licensed. The panel pairs with OVNode, the agent that runs OpenVPN on each VPN server.
